8. Robustness: The original FX H6 primary and matched-history comparison have negative DM statistics, while the Treasury primary has a positive statistic (Table 6). The FX H24 legacy has DM p=0.839 and HLN p=0.839, so its 1.83% descriptive improvement is not statistically significant at the 5% working-reference level. At the declared bandwidth, 19 of 72 Holm-adjusted working-reference p values fall below 5%, compared with 18 at doubled bandwidth. The declared-bandwidth count includes 15 favorable and 4 adverse mean differences for the conditional method. The matched FX H6 comparison has Holm p=2.86e-07; the Treasury primary has Holm p=0.32 and does not meet that family-adjusted threshold. Its descriptive loss deterioration remains an adverse finding. On the Treasury primary grid, 7/40 strict breaches yield POF p=0.00413 and CC p=0.0157. These coverage diagnostics assess different nulls from paired equal predictive loss.
8. Robustness: Figure 4 fixes τ=0.95 and varies the elementary-score threshold θ (Ehm et al., 2016). Both primary diagrams cross: QR has favorable and unfavorable threshold regions. Consequently neither report empirically dominates the other over the entire class of consistent 0.95-quantile scores. The check evaluates every unique forecast/outcome breakpoint privately; the displayed 201-point grid is an aggregate visualization. This differs from the archived preference frontier, which holds reports fixed and changes shortfall/excess weights. The calibration-and-sharpness perspective of Gneiting, Balabdaoui and Raftery (2007) motivates separate assessment of forecast concentration and calibration; the scalar capacity report addresses its stated functional.

Post-correction DQ instrument-basis clarification: the original diagnostic standardizes issued capacity across retained test rows. With an intercept this is a common invertible basis transformation when its standard deviation is finite/positive, leaving the same-row/same-HAC Wald statistic invariant in exact arithmetic. The raw issue-known basis defines the moment target; full-sample constants are not claimed available at issue. Three deterministic synthetic fixtures and12 affine variants were checked against an independent scalar HAC construction; no financial statistic/model was rerun and no raw p value changed. Singular/constant cases retain NA, floating-point boundary differences and all statistical reference/selection limits remain. The explicit proof and source hash are in post-correction-audit/dq-instrument-basis-audit.json.

Treasury intermediation likewise depends on dealer capacity (Duffie et al., 2023). A forecast of the maximum recorded position magnitude over a future horizon may support monitoring of the measured position: an endpoint can return toward its starting value after an intervening large position. Translating that monitoring signal into a particular margin or financing decision requires the corresponding contractual and balance-sheet inputs.\n\nWe ask whether mature conditional estimators improve forecasts of an absolute sampled-position peak relative to simple historical constructions. Every procedure predicts the same upper quantile of the same response on common issue origins. The historical alternatives use past headrooms, paths translated to the current signed position, or native peaks floored at the observed current magnitude. The conditional alternatives use ridge quantile regression, nearest-neighbor quantiles and scaled nearest-neighbor quantiles.\n\nThe matched-history FX regression comparison lowers mean loss by 14.77\\%, but increases breaches from 360 to 376. The original FX primary uses a different historical window and lowers loss by 12.66\\%. The separately declared Treasury primary deteriorates by 50.79\\%, with 54 rather than 28 breaches. Short-history FX regression also deteriorates at the longer horizon; a Treasury neighbor gain reverses on the sparse grid. These adverse outcomes are central findings.\n\nThe paper makes three contributions. First, it places established forecasting engines and historical constructions on a common completed-peak response with an explicit issue-known floor. Second, it controls completed-label pools and update schedules and retains the complete favorable and adverse model menu. Third, it documents how score, breach frequency, report coherence and fixed-report preferences can disagree across two financial measurement processes. The contribution is an application and model-validation benchmark using mature methods.\n\nSection 2 locates the study in the literature. Sections 3--5 describe data, forecasts and evaluation. Sections 6--7 report FX and Treasury results. Section 8 collects exploratory robustness evidence, Section 9 discusses mechanisms and limitations, and Section 10 concludes. Detailed historical menus, geometry and supplementary diagnostics appear in the appendices.\n\n\\section*{2. Related literature}\nWisniewski, Lindsay and Lindsay (2020) and the net-position forecasting chapter of Wisniewski (2024) are the closest empirical lineage. They already study conditional, neighbor and normalized endpoint forecasts on the FX source family, using lagged positions and calendar information. Here the response is a single upper quantile of a future absolute sampled maximum, including the current magnitude. Marginal endpoint intervals and their averaged losses address a different functional; the present comparison fits the established engines directly to completed peak labels.\n\nFinancial path extrema have a substantial prior literature. MaxVaR evaluates worst intermediate mark-to-market loss (Boudoukh et al., 2004). Liao and Theodosopoulos (2005) study the timing of mark-to-market for collateralized contingent credit exposure. Van den Hoogen (2017) models a conditional intraday liquidity buffer through the maximum cumulative payment deficit; Petrunia, Sabetti and Voia (2019) study a cross-participant end-of-day debit maximum. Arjani, Li and Sabetti (2020) forecast remaining-day liquidity-demand ratios. These targets clarify the specific contribution of a sampled net-position envelope.\n\nRegression quantiles (Koenker and Bassett, 1978), sequential neighbor quantiles (Biau and Patra, 2011), conditional historical filtering (Hull and White, 1998; Barone-Adesi et al., 1999), and quantile scoring (Gneiting, 2011) supply the mature methods. Quantile forests (Meinshausen, 2006), CAViaR (Engle and Manganelli, 2004), sequential conformal prediction (Xu and Xie, 2023), trajectory calibration (Zhou, Lindemann and Sesia, 2024) and expected-shortfall curves (Sözen, 2026) are further relevant alternatives. The executed estimator menu is deliberately bounded.\n\nThe resulting distinction is the measured peak response, known issue floor, completed-label timing, controlled history/update comparisons and qualified aggregate application. The benchmark measures how these mature procedures behave on the specified task; its supporting finite geometry explains construction differences.\n\n\\section*{3. Data}\nThe FX input is the one-hour member of the Net Position Time Series Dataset, version 2: 18,576 records from 5 February 2014 01:00 through 24 January 2017 00:00. Wisniewski et al. (2020) describe aggregate client-flow positions across five liquid currency pairs for one market maker. We use datetime and the signed NetPosUsd scalar, rather than reconstructing raw currency positions, hedge transactions or cash movements. The source has 18,420 one-hour and 155 forty-nine-hour adjacent gaps. We preserve chronology without sorting, removing gap-crossing windows or interpolation. Recorded-clock and vintage limits are collected in Section 9.\n\nThe Treasury application uses the New York Fed Primary Dealer Statistics series PDPOSGS-B: Treasury-bill long positions less short positions, measured at weekly Wednesday close in market/fair-value USD millions. The accepted snapshot contains 706 records. It combines dealer inventories, valuation and reporting composition. This supplies an aggregate financial measurement task alongside the individual market-maker client-flow series.\n\nTreasury validation issue dates are 24 July 2019 to 15 July 2020. The final \\(H=24\\) validation label ends at index 404 on 30 December 2020, before evaluation begins at 405 on 6 January 2021. The last common issue is 681 on 22 April 2026; its \\(H=6\\) label ends at 687 on 3 June, and \\(H=24\\) at 705 on 7 October 2026. FX validation ends at origin 11902; its latest \\(H=24\\) label ends at 11926, before evaluation origin 11927.\n\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n\\small\\textbf{Table 1. Target and forecasting methods}\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n\\small\\textbf{Notation. Distinct symbols for response, refits, history, distances and preferences.}\\par\\medskip\n\\centering\\fontsize{8}{10}\\selectfont\n\\begin{tabular}{lr}\n\\toprule\nSymbol & Definition \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\(N_t;\\ B_t\\) & Signed position; observed issue magnitude \\(|N_t|\\) \\\\\n\\(P_{t,H};\\ G_{t,H}\\) & Sampled absolute peak; headroom \\(P_{t,H}-B_t\\) \\\\\n\\(\\kappa(t);\\ W;\\ d\\) & Most recent refit index; label-pool size; refit step \\\\\n\\(C_t^m;\\ \\mathrm{Floor}\\) & Issued report for method m; the known-floor report \\\\\n\\(d_{\\rm abs};\\ d_{\\rm signed}\\) & Common-set anchor-distance radii \\\\\n\\(\\widetilde N_{i,h}^{\\rm tr};\\ M_{i,h}\\) & Translated historical path; AR residual-replay path \\\\\n\\(a_\\kappa;\\ z_{i,\\kappa}\\) & Training response scale; standardized predictors \\\\\n\\(a;\\ \\omega=a/(1-a)\\) & Shortfall weight; shortfall/excess preference ratio \\\\\n\\(\\mathcal J_\\lambda;\\ \\mathcal D_\\lambda\\) & Penalized regression objective; feasible dual objective \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{minipage}\n\\end{center}\nLet N denote the signed source-reported net position. The issue magnitude B is observed when the report is issued. Define the sampled peak P and its nonnegative headroom G by\n\n\\[\nB_t=|N_t|,\\qquad P_{t,H}=\\max_{0\\le h\\le H}|N_{t+h}|,\\qquad G_{t,H}=P_{t,H}-B_t\\ge0.\n\\]\nAt issue t, the most recent scheduled refit is \\(\\kappa\\)(t). Every training label is complete by that refit, and the next refit updates the transform, scale, coefficients and historical pool together:\n\n\\[\n\\kappa(t)=t_0+d\\left\\lfloor\\frac{t-t_0}{d}\\right\\rfloor,\\qquad\\mathcal T_{\\kappa,H,W}=\\{\\kappa-H-W+1,\\ldots,\\kappa-H\\}.\n\\]\nFor a completed episode i, let u and l be its largest and smallest increments from its starting position, including the zero increment. Translating its ordered path to \\(x=N_t\\) produces \\(V_{i,t}=\\max\\{x+u_i,-x-l_i\\}\\). On a common episode set A, Q selects the duplicate-preserving corrected empirical order statistic. The historical forecasts are\n\n\\[\nC^F_t=B_t+Q\\{G_{i,H}\\}_{i\\in\\mathcal A},\\qquad C^S_t=B_t+Q\\{V_{i,t}-B_t\\}_{i\\in\\mathcal A},\\qquad C^K_t=\\max\\{B_t,Q\\{P_{i,H}\\}_{i\\in\\mathcal A}\\}.\n\\]\nRolling controls update their completed-label set at each issue. Frozen controls use the same completed-label pool and refit schedule as the fitted procedures, while their current issue anchor continues to update. Earlier one-state controls retrieve nearby signed starting positions; their complete earlier menus remain in Appendix B.\n\nThe 33 raw coordinates are \\(N_t\\) through \\(N_{t-24}\\), current magnitude, short/long past increment RMS, sine/cosine of recorded hour, sine/cosine of weekday (Monday zero), and whether the just-observed adjacent gap exceeds its nominal interval. RMS spans are 24/168 FX records and 6/26 Treasury records; nominal gaps are 3600 and 604800 seconds. Calendar coordinates follow the stored source clock; constant training columns are centered exactly at their repeated value.\n\n\\[\nv_L(t)=\\left[\\frac1L\\sum_{j=t-L+1}^{t}(N_j-N_{j-1})^2\\right]^{1/2},\\qquad z_{i,\\kappa,j}=\\frac{x_{ij}-\\mu_{\\kappa j}}{s_{\\kappa j}}.\n\\]\nTraining-only centering and population standard deviations define z. An exactly constant coordinate receives unit scale after centering. Matching completed response origins retains the different past-only lookbacks required by the feature construction. The response scale a is computed from completed training headrooms and magnitudes:\n\n\\[\na_\\kappa=\\max\\left\\{\\frac1W\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal T}G_{i,H},\\;10^{-6}\\frac1W\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal T}|N_i|,\\;10^{-12}\\right\\}.\n\\]\nQR minimizes the normalized headroom regression-quantile objective with an unpenalized intercept and a ridge penalty on slopes. The fixed menu is \\(\\lambda\\in\\{0.001,0.01,0.1\\}\\); \\(\\tau=19/20\\). Training optimizes the unprojected response, while validation scores the final projected report in native units.\n\n\\[\n\\min_{\\beta_0,\\beta}\\frac1W\\sum_{i\\in\\mathcal T}\\rho_\\tau\\!\\left(\\frac{G_{i,H}}{a_\\kappa}-\\beta_0-z_{i,\\kappa}^{\\mathsf T}\\beta\\right)+\\frac\\lambda2\\|\\beta\\|_2^2.\n\\]\n\\[\nC_t^{QR}=B_t+\\max\\{0,a_\\kappa(\\widehat\\beta_{0,\\kappa}+z_{t,\\kappa}^{\\mathsf T}\\widehat\\beta_\\kappa)\\}.\n\\]\nThe intercept is unpenalized and slopes receive a ridge penalty. Adding B to a headroom quantile translates it into a peak quantile; projecting a report up to the known response floor weakly improves realized pinball loss. The equivalent peak parameterization and numerical conventions are retained in Appendix C.\n\nKNN uses training-standardized features with the frozen group weights and recency tie-breaking rule. It reports B plus a local headroom quantile. Scaled KNN divides each selected headroom by its past short RMS and multiplies the resulting quantile by the query RMS, using the same fixed stabilizer within each refit block.\n\n\\[\ns_{i\\mid \\kappa}=\\max\\{v_{\\rm short}(i),10^{-6}a_\\kappa\\},\\qquad C_t^{\\rm scaled}=B_t+s_{t\\mid \\kappa}Q_k\\{G_{i,H}/s_{i\\mid \\kappa}:i\\in\\mathcal N_{t,\\kappa,k}\\}.\n\\]\nThe neighbor menus are \\{180,360,720\\} at both FX windows, \\{20,40,52\\} at Treasury W52, and \\{40,80,160\\} at W260. The implementation uses exact order statistics and fails on an unavailable rank. For \\(k=52\\), \\(\\lceil(k+1)\\,0.95\\rceil=51\\), while the ordinary .95 empirical pinball quantile has rank 50. At W720, W2880 and W260, however, W times .95 is integer: the lower ordinary rank and the adjacent corrected rank are both endpoints of the empirical pinball minimizer interval. The W52 distinction is specific to its noninteger probability-times-pool-size case. A later endpoint/rank ablation is retained in Appendix D. Plain KNN at \\(k=W\\) equals frozen F exactly; membership is then the complete training pool. Scaled KNN still changes responses at \\(k=W\\). Long-window menus restrict neighborhood sizes below the full pool. Appendix C records numerical acceptance and failures.\n\n\\subsection*{Post-result / exploratory classical maximal-inequality benchmark}\nProposition 1 (classical Lévy bound, direct scalar application). Let the future real increments X\\textsubscript{1},\\ldots{},X\\textsubscript{H} be independent and individually symmetric about zero, with S\\textsubscript{h}=\\(\\sum\\)\\textsubscript{\\(j=1\\)}\\textsuperscript{h}X\\textsubscript{j}. They need not have the same distribution or finite moments. For a fixed starting position x, write \\(B=|x|\\) and q=inf\\{u:Pr(|S\\textsubscript{H}|\\(\\le\\)u)\\(\\ge\\)0.975\\}. Lévy's maximal inequality implies the following strict-breach bound; Appendix J gives the proof. This is a classical result applied to this target, not a new theorem (Sussman, 2023, Proposition3.4).\n\n\\[\n\\Pr\\!\\left(\\max_{0\\le h\\le H}|x+S_h|>B+q\\right)\\le\\Pr\\!\\left(\\max_{1\\le h\\le H}|S_h|>q\\right)\\le 2\\Pr(|S_H|>q)\\le0.05.\n\\]\nThe operational report L uses the same frozen completed-origin pool and refit times as F. Its endpoint sample is |N\\textsubscript{i+H}\\(-\\)N\\textsubscript{i}| and its one-based order rank is \\(\\lceil\\)39(W+1)/40\\(\\rceil\\). Add the resulting estimate to B\\textsubscript{t}. This empirical plug-in is distinct from the known population quantile in Proposition1. Overlapping endpoint samples and dependent, changing series do not inherit the proposition's population coverage. Conditional coverage additionally requires the independence and symmetry premises and the correct endpoint quantile conditional on issue information. The bound supplies no pinball-loss ordering against F.\n\n\\section*{5. Discussion and limitations}\n\\subsection*{Feature transport and the Treasury failure}\nThe hourly feature design transports awkwardly to the weekly Treasury task. Its 25 level coordinates span the current observation through 24 weeks of history. The two hour coordinates, two weekday coordinates and gap indicator are exactly constant on the weekly source. The original model has 33 predictors plus an intercept, or 34 coefficients, against \\(W=52\\) overlapping training labels in the shorter history. This is a high-dimensional fit relative to the available labels, rather than a \\(p>n\\) claim. All four Treasury penalty selections are menu endpoints. Its 52 validation origins contain at most 3 disjoint H24 label paths, a path count rather than an effective-sample-size estimate. Constant calendar coordinates, correlated levels, overlap and restricted tuning plausibly contribute to fragility; they remain hypotheses rather than causal findings.\n\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n\\small\\textbf{Table 8. Every original primary remains unchanged.}\\par\\medskip\n\\centering\\fontsize{8}{10}\\selectfont\n\\begin{tabular}{lrrrrrrr}\n\\toprule\nSource & H & W & \\(\\lambda\\) & \\(\\Delta\\) QR \\% & \\(\\Delta\\) F \\% & Breaches & Status \\\\\n\\midrule\nTreasury & 6 & 52 & 10 & -46.9 & -2.59 & 15 & COMPLETE \\\\\nTreasury & 6 & 260 & 10 & -32.2 & 2.17 & 32 & COMPLETE \\\\\nTreasury & 24 & 52 & 10 & -67.6 & 5.95 & 36 & COMPLETE \\\\\nTreasury & 24 & 260 & 10 & -52.3 & 0.11 & 15 & COMPLETE \\\\\nFX & 6 & 720 & 0.01 & 3.67 & 1.48 & 414 & COMPLETE \\\\\nFX & 6 & 2880 & 0.01 & 12.3 & -4.29 & 399 & COMPLETE \\\\\nFX & 24 & 720 & 0.01 & -11.4 & 16.5 & 701 & COMPLETE \\\\\nFX & 24 & 2880 & 0.01 & 0.898 & -2.89 & 508 & COMPLETE \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{minipage}\n\\end{center}\nThe four-predictor sensitivity uses B, signed N and short/long increment RMS, with validation penalties \\{0.001,0.01,0.1,1,10\\}. It lowers loss against the original QR in 5 of 8 cells and against matched F in 3 cells. In the Treasury primary cell its loss change is -32.2\\% relative to the original QR and 2.17\\% relative to F. All adverse cells remain in Table 8. The exercise changes features and the penalty menu jointly, so it measures a parsimonious specification sensitivity rather than identifying a feature-only cause or rehabilitating the original primary.\n\nThe contrast between the sources concerns a separately fitted procedure family: each source receives its own transforms, coefficient estimates, temporal scales and validation selection. The Treasury deterioration is an accuracy failure of the executed QR specifications. The exploratory AR comparison shows that the observed Treasury loss ranking differs across the executed families.\n\n\\subsection*{Limitations}\nThe FX evaluation interval was previously inspected, and the subsequent robustness analyses are post-result / exploratory. These records do not restore a compatible unseen dealer sample. Treasury is a downloaded-vintage, economic-date aggregate replay rather than an original-release public-information backtest; cross-dealer netting, valuation and composition distinguish it from an individual dealer's book.\n\nShared histories, overlapping labels, finite validation and investigator selection limit statistical generalization. The known floor can create an outcome atom: a valid upper quantile need not have exactly the nominal strict-breach probability. Numerical acceptance supplies no conditional-coverage guarantee. The horizon-specific mature scenario sets differ, so a zero observed crossing count cannot establish general coherence.\n\nStipulated shortfall/excess weights are not observed financing prices. Quotes, fills, hedges, book decomposition, collateral and cash flows would be required to map this passive envelope into an operational inventory, margin or funding policy. This study evaluates forecasts, not such interventions; Avellaneda and Stoikov (2008) provide a distinct active inventory-sensitive quoting framework.\n\nThe strongest alternatives extend beyond the executed menu, including quantile forests, CAViaR, sequential conformal procedures and full volatility-filtered historical simulation. Same completed-label pools and update schedules improve procedural comparability while allowing differences in feature lookback, regularization, scaling and validation. Future compatible observations and decision-linked inputs would test broader portability.\n\nA post-result / exploratory selected-fit readback examines the Treasury C2 menu boundary directly (Appendix I). At \\(\\lambda=10\\), standardized response-normalized slope norms range from 0.001497 to 0.01937. Removing slopes while keeping each fitted intercept changes capacity by a mean absolute 136.8--832.3 source USD millions across the four cells. Relative to the lower empirical headroom-quantile report I, observed loss is 0.2432--2.192\\% lower; this descriptive difference has no dedicated selection-adjusted test. The fits have small normalized slopes and high headroom correlation with I, but are not identical to I or F. A boundary penalty and high capacity correlation do not by themselves demonstrate zero feature value. Three of the four C2 cells still have higher loss than F.\n\nThe expanded aggregate panel strengthens the negative transport finding but does not isolate its mechanism. Features and tuning menus, finite sample size, target behavior and reporting-regime changes can all matter. Downloaded cross-era histories are not original-release vintages; metadata/provenance for each key are retained. A prospective public-release protocol freezes the four procedures and selected historical-validation penalties before future issue artifacts. The first planned new release is after the protocol freeze, rather than retroactively labeling the already published October14 observation as unseen. Because the release clock lags economic dates, the target includes prediction of unpublished measurements, with a nowcast/forecast mixture. Results await prior timestamped report issuance and target publication; no live prospective validation is claimed.\n\n\\section*{10. Conclusion}\nMature conditional estimators change the historical ranking on the sampled FX peak task, while the Treasury regression primary deteriorates. Matched-history FX H6 QR lowers mean loss by 14.77\\% and raises breaches from 360 to 376; the Treasury primary raises loss by 50.79\\% and breaches from 28 to 54. Short-history QR deterioration and the sparse-grid Treasury neighbor reversal remain central adverse findings. The exploratory AR, rank, preference and coherence comparisons show why score improvements, breach frequency and report shape should be evaluated together. The study contributes a controlled application and model-validation benchmark for measured position peaks. Its next evidential step is compatible new financial observations and an explicit decision mapping.\n\nThe exploratory 12-series extension also finds higher loss than F in 45/48 QR33 cells and 37/48 parsimonious cells, further limiting general performance claims.\n\n\\section*{Appendix A. Finite geometry and its predictive limits}\nOn a common set and fixed rank, let \\(d_{\\rm abs}=\\max_{i\\in J}\\bigl|B-|N_i|\\bigr|\\) and \\(d_{\\rm signed}=\\max_{i\\in J}|x-N_i|\\). Elementary order-statistic and projection stability gives \\(|F-K|\\le d_{\\rm abs}\\), \\(|S-K|\\le d_{\\rm signed}\\), hence \\(|F-S|\\le d_{\\rm abs}+d_{\\rm signed}\\). Appendix A proves these finite relationships and their predictive limits. Nearest signed-state membership minimizes its maximum signed distance at a given count; it need not minimize forecast loss. These statements do not automatically bound QR, scaled responses or the richer 33-coordinate distance.\n\n\\subsection*{A.1. Common-set projection bounds}\nThese construction arguments concern F/S/K on an identical historical set and rank. They are retained from the earlier comparison. A one-dimensional signed-distance minimax property does not extend automatically to the multivariate neighbor distance, and the bounds do not automatically constrain QR or scale-adjusted responses.\n\nThese are elementary finite-array arguments, rather than new asymptotic or coverage results. Fix a nonempty common selected set J, an available rank \\(1\\le k\\le|J|\\), query \\(x=N_t\\), floor \\(B=|x|\\) and completed historical windows. All identities in this appendix concern real arithmetic. Write \\(B_i=|N_i|\\), \\(d_{i,h}=N_{i+h}-N_i\\), with \\(d_{i,0}=0\\), and define\n\nLet \\(a_i=\\min_h d_{i,h}\\) and \\(b_i=\\max_h d_{i,h}\\), so \\(a_i\\le0\\le b_i\\). These are the lower and upper increments denoted l and u in Section 4. The auxiliary nonnegative envelope coordinates below use \\(u_i=b_i\\) and \\(v_i=-a_i\\).\n\n\\[\nA_i=B+P_i-B_i,\\qquad T_i=\\max_{0\\le h\\le H}|x+d_{i,h}|,\\qquad C_B(z)=\\max(B,z).\n\\]\nBoth \\(A_i\\) and \\(T_i\\) are at least B. The projection \\(C_B\\) is nondecreasing and 1-Lipschitz. It commutes with a finite order statistic, as does a common translation. Hence \\(F_J=Q_k(A)\\), \\(S_J=Q_k(T)\\) and \\(K_J=Q_k(C_B(P))\\). Since \\(C_B(A_i)=A_i\\),\n\n\\[\n|A_i-C_B(P_i)|\\le |A_i-P_i|=|B-B_i|.\n\\]\nThe reverse triangle inequality bounds each path value's change under a starting-position translation by \\(|x-N_i|\\). Taking a maximum gives \\(|T_i-P_i|\\le|x-N_i|\\). Applying the same floor projection preserves that bound because \\(T_i\\ge B\\). Finally, paired order statistics are nonexpansive in the maximum coordinate difference: if \\(|u_i-v_i|\\le r\\) for every i, then \\(u_i\\le v_i+r\\) and conversely; monotonicity and common translation give \\(|Q_k(u)-Q_k(v)|\\le r\\). These observations prove the two common-set K bounds stated above. The triangle inequality and \\(\\bigl||N_i|-|x|\\bigr|\\le|N_i-x|\\) prove the stated F/S bound. Keeping the rank fixed while changing one side's historical rows does not by itself justify these common-set comparison bounds.\n\nAmong all size-m subsets, selecting the m smallest signed distances minimizes the largest selected distance: any alternative must include an element at least as far away as the mth ordered distance. This finite minimax fact, with the declared tie convention, concerns the signed radius. It does not minimize the absolute-anchor radius, the sum of the two radii, the actual report gap or a forecast loss. For every fixed realized y, pinball loss is \\(\\max(\\tau,1-\\tau)\\)-Lipschitz in its report, so a report-gap bound also bounds the absolute loss difference. Such stability supplies no sign for the realized or expected loss difference.\n\n\\subsection*{A.2. Envelope plateaus and the role of signed anchors}\nPut \\(u_i=b_i\\ge0\\) and \\(v_i=-a_i\\ge0\\). The headroom of an increment envelope at any anchor z is\n\n\\[\ng_i(z)=\\max(z+u_i,-z+v_i)-|z|=\\begin{cases}\\max(u_i,v_i-2z),&z\\ge0,\\\\\\max(u_i+2z,v_i),&z\\le0.\\end{cases}\n\\]\nF pools each envelope's headroom at its historical anchor, \\(g_i(N_i)\\); S pools its headroom at the query, \\(g_i(x)\\). The branches agree at zero and together make \\(g_i\\) 2-Lipschitz, with range lying in \\([\\min(u_i,v_i),\\max(u_i,v_i)]\\). Apply the distance and range bounds to each paired row, then use the same-rank order-statistic stability from A.1 to obtain\n\n\\[\n|F_J-S_J|\\le\\max_{i\\in J}\\min\\{2|x-N_i|,|u_i-v_i|\\}.\n\\]\nFor example, \\(u_i=v_i\\) in every row makes \\(F_J=S_J\\) at arbitrary anchors. Nonnegative query/source anchors together with \\(u_i\\ge v_i\\) in every row also suffice; the nonpositive analogue uses \\(v_i\\ge u_i\\). These are sufficient conditions, not a characterization: pooled order statistics can coincide even when paired rows differ. The range bound also gives \\(F_J,S_J\\le R_J\\), where \\(R_J=B+Q_k\\{\\max(u_i,v_i):i\\in J\\}\\). This is a theoretical same-set ordering; no R retrieval configuration is evaluated in the extension, and the ordering does not make \\(R_J\\) preferable under a given loss.\n\nIf every \\(B_i\\le B\\), then \\(A_i\\ge C_B(P_i)\\) and \\(F_J\\ge K_J\\). If every \\(B_i\\ge B\\), then \\(C_B(P_i)=P_i\\ge A_i\\) and \\(F_J\\le K_J\\). Equal absolute anchors force F=K but leave signs relevant to S. A coherent full-pool example uses \\(c>0\\), \\(H=1\\), \\(n=720\\), \\(\\tau=19/20\\), \\(t=721\\) and \\(N_s=(-1)^{s+1}c\\) for \\(0\\le s\\le721\\). The pool uses completed labels at origins \\(J=\\{1,\\ldots,720\\}\\), with 360 anchors of each sign and current \\(N_t=c\\). All native peaks equal c and headrooms equal zero, so F=K=c. Raw reanchoring gives 360 peaks c and 360 peaks 3c; rank 685 gives S=3c. Thus \\(d_{\\rm abs}=0\\) while \\(d_{\\rm signed}=2c\\) and \\(|S-K|=2c\\). At each original refit \\(\\kappa\\), put \\(i_0=\\kappa-H-W+1\\).\n\n\\[\nN_s=c_\\kappa+\\phi_\\kappa N_{s-1}+\\epsilon_s.\n\\]\nFit on the unique transitions \\(i_0+1,\\ldots,\\kappa\\). The W completed scenarios have \\(W+H\\) levels in their union and \\(W+H-1\\) unique transitions; overlapping paths do not duplicate transitions in OLS. Coefficients and the historical pool remain fixed until the next original refit, while the query uses the actual \\(N_t\\).\n\nUsing the same fitted coefficients for every residual in a block and replaying its original order from x=\\(N_t\\) gives the replay identity\n\n\\[\nM_{i,h}(x)=N_{i+h}+\\phi_\\kappa^h(x-N_i).\n\\]\nSet \\(h=0\\) explicitly to x and report the corrected empirical quantile of the W maximum absolute replay paths. The intercept cancels in this deterministic identity; it is still estimated in the mean recursion. At exact \\(\\phi_\\kappa=1\\) the arithmetic agrees with frozen S. Negative or above-one finite estimates are eligible, without clipping. Constant regressors, lost dispersion and nonfinite computations fail without a substitute model.\n\nThis is a mean-filtered ordered-block historical comparison, not the full conditional-volatility filtered simulation of Hull and White (1998) or Barone-Adesi et al. (1999). It does not standardize/rescale innovations, fit GARCH, independently draw future steps or introduce Monte Carlo randomness. Conditional representativeness of historical residual blocks remains unverified; numerical OLS acceptance supplies no coverage or mean-reversion law. Appendix A.4 gives the path relationship, and Appendix C records numerical checks.\n\n\\subsection*{AR annual and sparse-grid sensitivity}\nDirect-S signs reverse for FX H24 W720 on the 265-origin grid (+2.386\\% overall, \\(-\\)1.884\\% sparse) and Treasury H24 W52 on only 12 origins (+35.125\\%, \\(-\\)14.100\\%). Treasury H24 W260 remains favorable on its sparse grid but is adverse in 2022 and 2023 (+9.928\\%, +20.224\\%). Every annual and sparse contrast remains. Observed fitted coefficients lie between zero and one, with refit means around .981--.985 for FX and .676--.850 for Treasury; these descriptions do not identify true mean reversion. Source, horizon, history and model family all matter, and neither average report reduction nor a below-one slope determines a loss ranking.\n\n\\section*{Appendix G. Complete post-result inference and specification outputs}\nThe complete machine-readable DM, HLN, doubled-bandwidth,72-family Holm, sparse-grid coverage and full-sample DQ-type results are retained in results/revision-20261023/inference/. Each NA retains an explicit reason. The accompanying scripts and known-answer tests are supplied together. The exact replicated six-table audit and source identities are in recovery/. Raw FX data and origin-level traces remain private.\n\nThe HAC covariance uses centered moment products with denominator n. DQ instruments are the intercept, four matured hit lags and standardized issue-known capacity; its chi-square reference has six degrees of freedom when full rank. The covariance must be finite, full rank and positive definite. The doubled bandwidth remains much shorter than the longest training history, so this limited check does not establish adequate long-run covariance calibration. Sparse grid tests remove overlapping target windows but retain shared training dependence. Treasury grid sizes of40 or12 are particularly weak for asymptotic reference calibration. The equality-based POF, CC and DQ diagnostics require exact5\\% moments; a quantile with atoms can validly be conservative, so rejection by low hit frequency differs from undercoverage. Missing transition-state rows render independence and CC unidentified. HLN was derived for mean-squared-error comparisons; pinball p values are approximate. Holm familywise control requires valid component p values: the adjustment does not validate the working DM references or remove post-inspection selection. All analyses are post-result and reuse inspected samples.\n\nThe DQ-type null is \\(\\mathbb E[Z_t(I_t-0.05)]=0\\) for the six declared instruments, including the intercept. Rejection concerns these moments; nonrejection leaves other conditional departures untested. The original out-of-sample CAViaR theorem assumes growing estimation and evaluation samples with their evaluation-to-estimation ratio tending to zero. The fixed-window, overlapping-target HAC calculation here is a specified adaptation rather than a direct application of that theorem.\n\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{minipage}{\\linewidth}\n\\small\\textbf{Table H1. Classical bound proof and exploratory L outputs}\nProof of Proposition1. Let M=max|S\\textsubscript{h}| and let \\(\\eta\\) be the first h with |S\\textsubscript{h}|\\( > \\)c. These tests retain their finite dependent-sample, reference-law and post-result limitations.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'## Independent validation remains incomplete'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'The expanded panel has '"'"'+str(panel['"'"'series_count'"'"'])+'"'"' related aggregate series, '"'"'+str(panel['"'"'QR33'"'"']['"'"'total_cells'"'"'])+'"'"' H/W cells and '"'"'+str(panel['"'"'rows'"'"'])+'"'"' procedure outputs. QR33 has higher loss than F in '"'"'+str(panel['"'"'QR33'"'"']['"'"'higher_loss_than_F'"'"'])+'"'"'/'"'"'+str(panel['"'"'QR33'"'"']['"'"'total_cells'"'"'])+'"'"' cells; parsimonious QR has higher loss in '"'"'+str(panel['"'"'C2_QR4'"'"']['"'"'higher_loss_than_F'"'"'])+'"'"'/'"'"'+str(panel['"'"'C2_QR4'"'"']['"'"'total_cells'"'"'])+'"'"' cells. This broadens the evidence of specification/transport fragility across the available aggregate tasks. It is not a compatible unseen second dealer: the series share dealer reporting and economic regimes, and the panel is not a set of independent trials.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'The original Treasury source is independently compiled relative to the FX source but measures a different aggregate. Netting, valuation and reporting composition matter. Downloaded cross-era economic-date histories are not original-release information vintages. The future release-clock protocol supplies no actual issued forecast or mature future label. Its required capture, prefix-only issuance and missing-week adapter has not been implemented or validated. The current historical batch API still requires an outcome suffix even though its fitted/query slices use only mature/observed values.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'## The corrected AR mechanism test'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'The fitted financial coefficients are level-AR descriptions. Differenced stationary levels have negatively correlated increments and are not themselves the originally simulated positive-increment AR model. Both old positive-increment cases and the new level/negative-increment cases are retained. The centered Gaussian population-threshold simulations are illustrative mechanism checks, not a calibrated replication of either financial source. Fixed tail starts using a stationary-marginal endpoint threshold are distinguished from conditional-endpoint oracle thresholds.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'The negative-increment case with an observed rate just above nominal is within Monte Carlo uncertainty and supplies no demonstrated population violation. All tested level cases are conservative in these simulations; that does not extend the independent-symmetric theorem to all mean-reverting processes. Empirical dependent training-pool L outputs retain their adverse cells and have no uniform loss/conservativeness ordering.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'## Remaining methodological and economic limits'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'- Both original primary Murphy curves cross. Neither dominates across the consistent-score class for the stipulated quantile; one pinball mean is only one preference-sensitive criterion.'"'"','"'"'- The FX evaluation record had already been inspected. Original public execution/selection chronology and later local before-run bindings do not undo earlier investigator selection. All new empirical supplements remain post-result / exploratory.'"'"','"'"'- DM/HAC, sparse POF/CC/DQ and Holm arithmetic are checkable, but their dependence, moment, exact-hit-probability and working-reference premises are additional conditions. The known floor can create atoms; sparse Treasury grids are small; adjusting p values does not validate those p values.'"'"','"'"'- C2 changes the predictor set and penalty menu jointly and repeatedly reaches the menu boundary. Its slopes are not exactly zero and it is not identical to I/F; no selection-adjusted evidence isolates conditional feature value or identifies why the original QR failed.'"'"','"'"'- The loss preference is stipulated rather than measured financing cost. Passive position-envelope accuracy does not establish a margin, funding, hedging or quoting policy benefit. Such a claim requires the relevant cash flows, risk decomposition, control actions and economic costs.'"'"','"'"'- Public code/result identities, causal fixtures and numerical certificates make the implementation more assessable. They cannot establish estimator consistency, distributional coverage or economic usefulness. Exact financial replay still requires the accepted raw FX bytes, whose redistribution permission is unverified.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'## Publication-level assessment'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'There is insufficient basis to promise a journal tier or acceptance. A major methodological contribution is not supported by this version: its engines and inequalities are mature, and exact target-combination priority has not been established. A narrowly framed applied-risk or model-validation submission would still need an editor and reviewers to find the financial measurement use case and controlled negative findings useful enough. It should not be sold as a generally superior forecasting method.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'The most consequential next evidence is compatible new financial observations and a clear decision-linked use case, followed by a sufficiently fair predeclared challenge from the relevant mature alternatives. More diagnostics on the same inspected record or another cosmetic revision cannot substitute for those. No further data/model work is silently proposed or run by this assessment.'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'## Evidence and scope'"'"','"'"''"'"','"'"'Machine-readable current counts and exact input hashes are in `../results/revision-20261023/round2/post-correction-audit/quality-assessment-current-facts.json`. The companion static audits separately record their actual read ranges and authorship roles. Dated original evidence maps and archived scientific results are unchanged. This note changes no primary, forecast, selected parameter, numerical result, paper PDF or seven-hour completion status.'"'"','"'"''"'"']
